title: Current Affairs World II
desc: Organisations, treaties, summits and international days

questions.q: The United Nations was founded in:
questions.e: The UN Charter came into force on 24 October 1945; UN Day is observed on 24 October.

questions.q: The UN headquarters is in:
questions.e: Geneva, Vienna and Nairobi host major UN offices.

questions.q: The number of permanent members of the UN Security Council is:
questions.e: USA, UK, France, Russia and China; there are ten non-permanent members elected for two years, so fifteen in total.

questions.q: The current UN Secretary-General (since 2017) is:
questions.e: He started his second term on 1 January 2022; his term ends on 31 December 2026.

questions.q: The UN General Assembly has how many member states?
questions.e: South Sudan joined in 2011 as the 193rd member.

questions.q: The International Court of Justice sits at:
questions.e: The ICJ is the principal judicial organ of the UN.

questions.q: The International Criminal Court is also at:
questions.e: The ICC was established by the Rome Statute (2002). Pakistan is not a party to it.

questions.q: The World Health Organization is headquartered in:
questions.e: WHO was established on 7 April 1948, celebrated as World Health Day.

questions.q: UNICEF was established in:
questions.e: It was created to give emergency food and healthcare to children after World War II. It won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1965.

questions.q: UNICEF headquarters is in:
questions.e: It works for the rights of children in over 190 countries.

questions.q: The UN Convention on the Rights of the Child was adopted in:
questions.e: Pakistan ratified it in November 1990.

questions.q: UNESCO headquarters is in:
questions.e: It deals with education, science and culture.

questions.q: FAO headquarters is in:
questions.e: FAO leads international efforts against hunger.

questions.q: The ILO headquarters is in:
questions.e: The ILO was founded in 1919 and is the oldest UN specialised agency.

questions.q: The International Monetary Fund is headquartered in:
questions.e: The IMF and World Bank were established at the Bretton Woods conference (1944).

questions.q: The World Trade Organization is headquartered in:
questions.e: WTO succeeded GATT in 1995.

questions.q: The OPEC headquarters is in:
questions.e: OPEC was founded in 1960 in Baghdad.

questions.q: The OIC (Organisation of Islamic Cooperation) headquarters is in:
questions.e: The OIC was founded in 1969 after the arson attack on Al-Aqsa Mosque.

questions.q: The Arab League headquarters is in:
questions.e: Founded in 1945.

questions.q: NATO was formed in:
questions.e: Headquarters in Brussels. It has 32 members after Finland (2023) and Sweden (2024) joined.

questions.q: The European Union headquarters is in:
questions.e: The euro is used by 20 members; Croatia joined the eurozone in 2023 and Bulgaria is to join in 2026.

questions.q: Brexit took effect on:
questions.e: The UK voted to leave in the 2016 referendum; the transition ended on 31 December 2020.

questions.q: SAARC was founded in:
questions.e: SAARC headquarters is Kathmandu. It has eight members: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.

questions.q: The ASEAN headquarters is in:
questions.e: ASEAN was founded in 1967.

questions.q: The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Secretariat is in:
questions.e: Pakistan and India became full members in 2017.

questions.q: BRICS includes Brazil, Russia, India, China and:
questions.e: It expanded in 2024 to include Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the UAE; Indonesia joined in 2025.

questions.q: The G7 does NOT include:
questions.e: G7 members are the USA, UK, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and Canada.

questions.q: The G20 summit of 2023 was held in:
questions.e: The African Union was made a permanent member. The 2024 summit was in Rio de Janeiro, and the 2025 summit in Johannesburg.

questions.q: The COP28 climate conference (2023) was held in:
questions.e: COP29 was in Baku (2024) and COP30 in Belem, Brazil (2025).

questions.q: The Paris Climate Agreement was adopted in:
questions.e: It aims to limit warming to well below 2 C, preferably 1.5 C.

questions.q: The Kyoto Protocol was adopted in:
questions.e: It set binding emission targets for developed countries.

questions.q: The Rio Earth Summit was held in:
questions.e: The 1972 Stockholm conference was the first major UN conference on the environment.

questions.q: International Children's Day (in many countries) is observed on:
questions.e: Many countries celebrate on 1 June; 20 November is Universal Children's Day.

questions.q: International Women's Day is observed on:
questions.e: It has been observed since 1911 and recognised by the UN in 1977.

questions.q: Human Rights Day is observed on:
questions.e: It commemorates the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948).

questions.q: International Labour Day is observed on:
questions.e: Also called May Day.

questions.q: World Literacy Day is observed on:
questions.e: Declared by UNESCO in 1966.

questions.q: World Population Day is observed on:
questions.e: Marked since 1989.

questions.q: World Refugee Day is observed on:
questions.e: It honours refugees worldwide.

questions.q: The International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women is:
questions.e: It begins 16 days of activism ending on Human Rights Day.

questions.q: The World Bank headquarters is in:
questions.e: Pakistan has been a member since 1950.

questions.q: Asian Development Bank headquarters is in:
questions.e: ADB was established in 1966.

questions.q: Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) headquarters is in:
questions.e: AIIB is led by China and began operations in 2016.

questions.q: The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded in:
questions.e: The other Nobel prizes are awarded in Stockholm.

questions.q: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted in:
questions.e: It was adopted by the UN General Assembly on 10 December 1948 in Paris.

questions.q: Which UN agency is responsible for refugees?
questions.e: UNHCR won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1954 and 1981.

questions.q: Which UN organ has the power to impose binding sanctions?
questions.e: The five permanent members have veto power.

questions.q: The UN Population Fund is abbreviated as:
questions.e: UNDP is the UN Development Programme.

questions.q: The UN Environment Programme headquarters is in:
questions.e: It was founded in 1972.

questions.q: The World Food Programme won the Nobel Peace Prize in:
questions.e: It is headquartered in Rome.
